subject: Hosted evaluation: quickstart, rate limits, SLA burst questions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dawson <claire@finwave.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + hosted evaluation next steps

Claire—

Thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get your team running on Hosted for an initial evaluation:

What we heard
- Primary goal: integrate semantic search + summarization into your underwriting workflow.
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for typical requests; average prompt ~300 tokens.
- Traffic: steady-state ~40 rps, burst up to 150rps during batch reindexes.
- Data residency: US only for now (legal is confirming).

Hosted fit
- Hosted API supports region pinning (we can keep eval traffic in us-east-1).
- For initial eval we usually recommend Hosted (fastest to onboard). Dedicated is recommended once you need predictable sustained throughput with committed GPUs.

Trial limits / quickstart
- Sandbox credentials: we can provision a sandbox project with two endpoints (search, summarize).
- Default trial rate limits: 5 rps per endpoint; account-level soft cap 50 rps. These are adjustable for short-term bursts—send a request and we can raise to 150rps for a 48h window.
- Prefix/KV caching is available and we can share config suggestions based on your prompt shapes.

Next steps
1) I’ll provision sandbox creds and send links + quickstart guide (hosted-quickstart-checklist.xlsx attached).
2) Mina will copy in security artifacts (SOC 2) and answer compliance questions.
3) Follow-up call w/ infra + solutions to map endpoints and canary plan (propose Thurs 10am PT).

Attachments: hosted-quickstart-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
(415) 555-0182
From: Claire Dawson <claire@finwave.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + hosted evaluation next steps

Ben,

Thanks — that all looks reasonable. A few clarifying questions before the follow-up:

- Data residency: we need all data to remain in the US; will Hosted guarantee that for the eval project? Any logs that leave region?
- Burst increases: can we get a guaranteed short-term bump to 150rps or is that manual each time?
- Canary strategy: what support do you provide for gradual traffic ramp and automatic fallback to a lighter model if latency spikes?
- Security artifacts: can you send a redacted SOC 2 report and an audit contact? Procurement will also need a basic SOW template.

Claire
Claire Dawson
Head of Product, FinWave
claire@finwave.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dawson <claire@finwave.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 18:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + hosted evaluation next steps

Hi Claire — thanks for the questions; answered inline below.

> Data residency: will Hosted guarantee that for the eval project? Any logs that leave region?
We can pin the evaluation project to us-east-1 and restrict egress to that region for model inference. Control plane metadata (billing/usage analytics) is routed through our control plane in the US as well. We do not replicate customer prompt text to other regions. I'll attach a redacted SOC 2 report (SOC2-report-redacted.pdf) and include an audit contact (audit@redwood.com).

> Burst increases: can we get a guaranteed short-term bump to 150rps or is that manual each time?
Short answer: we can grant a time-limited burst increase. For evals we typically approve a 48-hour 150rps bump via an internal support ticket; for production-grade guarantees we recommend Dedicated with committed capacity and an SLA. I'll start the support ticket now; expect confirmation within 4 hours.

> Canary strategy: what support do you provide for gradual traffic ramp and automatic fallback to a lighter model if latency spikes?
We provide built-in rollout policies in the Console: canary percentages, automatic latency/error thresholds, and model fallback rules (e.g., route to a quantized variant or smaller family). Soojin (solutions) can run a short session with your infra team to craft the canary plan.

> Procurement: SOW template
Attached: hosted-quickstart-checklist.xlsx (from Ben) and a simple SOW template can be shared after we confirm scope. Procurement contact — procurement@finwave.ai — I'll loop in after the sandbox is provisioned.

Next steps (concrete):
- Ben: will provision sandbox creds (target: within 24 hours).
- Mina: attached SOC2-report-redacted.pdf and opening support ticket for 48h 150rps burst.
- Soojin: propose a 30-min canary planning session Thurs 10am PT (I’ll send a calendar invite).

Links:
- Quickstart docs: https://redwood.example.com/docs/hosted-quickstart
- SOC2: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2

If that sounds good I’ll move the support ticket and send the sandbox link.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com
